rounds.text: Dhanuka Infra Realty Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.52x [E2] and a P/E ratio of 9.7x [E1], both of which sit well below sector benchmarks [E6, E7]. The company has achieved a robust cash conversion of 1.78x, ensuring that reported profits are fully backed by actual cash flow [E31]. Furthermore, the balance sheet is exceptionally strong, featuring a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and a comfortable current ratio of 5.61x [E34, E35]. While the stock has suffered a 59% decline over the past year [E22], a discounted cash flow analysis suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 38 per share, implying a substantial margin of safety of 76.0% [E40, E41]. Conceded: the company has delivered poor long-term sales growth of -26% [E14, E52], and promoter holdings have decreased by 23.81 percentage points since 2020 [E38]. Despite these historical headwinds, the company is demonstrating a clear turnaround with quarterly operating margins improving by 196 percentage points year-over-year [E28].
